reason: RUNBOOK 6.5: three laps in one session. Not a stop — the successor continues from the gate. Context, not quota, is the limit the gate cannot see.
did: Lap 3 replaced the invented 0.5%-per-run reservation with a bound measured from data the repo already held: the git history of state/claude-usage.json joined with the lap timestamps in state/laps.json (scripts/derive-lap-cost.mjs). Reading it back caught a second problem and it was fixed in the same lap.

observed_not_guessed.derived_bound: 1 point across 6 laps over 2.87h -> <= 0.1667%/lap. Two collections later the same span reads 2 points across 7 laps -> <= 0.2857%/lap. The number moves with the data.
observed_not_guessed.gate_effect_measured: reserve 30.10% -> 26.67% and no longer capped; discretionary 12.90% -> 16.33%; lap budget 1.39% -> 1.77%. Read from the gate output, not predicted.
observed_not_guessed.first_usable_sample_was_a_trap: lap 3 closed with a real 1.000% delta — the first sample in twelve to pass every check — and it was wrong to trust. Weekly readings are whole points, so a 1-point delta has 100% relative error. It is 3.5x the derived bound over the same period, and pacing prefers a sample over a bound, so it would have won. Verified the harm before acting: automations.json had already been written to 1%, and at 33 runs that reserves 33% against revenue-loop instead of 9.43%. record-lap now refuses a delta below 2 points as at_measurement_quantum and keeps observed_delta_percent so nothing is lost. Registry re-checked after: back to null.
observed_not_guessed.cap_did_its_job: MAX_RESERVED_FRACTION would have limited the damage to a halved discretionary rather than a deadlock. The existing guard worked; it just should not have needed to.

next_lap_should: Two things are ready, and neither is more instrumentation. (1) pacing throttles on observed 39.7%/day computed over the whole elapsed window, but the burn measured over the last 3 hours is 16.3%/day. It has been reporting ahead_of_pace_throttle all session while the recent rate is close to flat pace. derive-lap-cost.mjs already emits burn_percent_per_day per span; using the recent rate instead of the window average would stop throttling on stale history. (2) Nothing runs derive-lap-cost.mjs on a schedule, so the bound only refreshes when a lap remembers to. It belongs in the usage-monitor workflow next to the collector. Beyond those, the ETA candidates are untouched and every channel is still infinite — vscode_extension_pro is top of the list at 3-14 days to first yen.
known_gap: push-with-retry.sh runs git pull --rebase without --autostash, so it fails whenever state/laps.json holds an open lap, which is always mid-lap. It cost four manual recoveries this session. Also: commit a7aa385 reached main with the placeholder message tmp-derived; 535710b documents it, because rewriting main is correctly blocked here.
archive_policy: A successor archives its predecessor at startup, and only when get_session reports SESSION_STATUS_IDLE. A session cannot archive itself: doing so stops it before its own final record is written. 'I spawned you' does not mean 'I have finished' — the predecessor may still be committing.
